issue_context.title: BUG: groupby with dropna=False and pa.dictionary drops NA values
issue_context.body:
```python
df = pd.DataFrame({'A': ['a1', pd.NA]}, dtype=pd.ArrowDtype(pa.dictionary(pa.int32(), pa.utf8())))
print(df.groupby("A", dropna=False)[["A"]].first())
#      A
# A     
# a1  a1
```

There should be a 2nd row with the NA value since `dropna=False`.

review_comments: `dictionary_decode()` works on the `DictionaryArray` while the input to `factorize()` function is a `ChunkedArray`. So the chunked array first needs to be combined into a dictionary array and then the `dictionary_decode()` can be used on it which i think is more inefficient as compared to simply casting the array to its underlying data type.

I think you're explaining why you have the cast here, but I'm not quite understanding it. Can you give a bit more details (just as a response here, and we can decide if the comment should be updated later).

If the input array is already a dictionary array then the dictionary encode function does nothing and hence the null_encoding parameter is ignored
https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/generated/pyarrow.compute.dictionary_encode.html
Casting the array and then re-encoding it, ensures the proper use of null_encoding when NA values are desired in the output

Am I correct in that this only needs to be done for `pyarrow<15.0.0`? If that is the case, then can you do this conditionally based on the version of PyArrow available.

    from pandas.compat.pyarrow import pa_version_under15p0

This type casting actually needs to be done irrespective of the pyarrow version to ensure the use of null_encoding. In the older versions of pyarrow, you would get an error if you attempted to encode an already dictionary encoded array and that's why there was this if block to simply bypass the encoding operation but it wasn't applying the null_encoding parameter. 
```
if pa.types.is_dictionary(data.type):
    encoded = data
```

Maybe there are other ways to do this but I could only find this one

I mentioned this on Arrow's repo: https://github.com/apache/arrow/issues/34890#issuecomment-2638196242

In the meantime, I think this work around is okay, but going to test it a bit on my end in the next day or two.
